{{no footnotes|date=November 2016}}

In [[numerical analysis]], '''interpolative decomposition (ID)''' factors a [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] as the product of two matrices, one of which contains selected columns from the original matrix, and the other of which has a subset of columns consisting of the [[identity matrix]] and all its values are no greater than&nbsp;2 in absolute value.

==Definition ==
Let <math> A </math> be an <math> m \times n </math> matrix of [[Rank (linear algebra)|rank]] <math> r </math>.  The matrix <math> A </math> can be written as
:<math> A = A_{(:,J)} X , \, </math>
where
* <math> J </math> is a subset of <math> r </math> indices from <math>\{ 1 ,\ldots, n  \};</math>
* The <math> m \times r </math> matrix <math> A_{(:,J)} </math> represents <math> J</math>'s columns of <math> A;</math>
* <math> X </math> is an <math> r \times n </math> matrix, all of whose values are less than 2 in magnitude. <math> X </math>  has an <math> r \times r </math> identity submatrix.

Note that a similar decomposition can be done using the rows of <math> A </math> instead of its columns.

== Example ==
Let <math> A </math> be the <math> 3 \times 3 </math> matrix of rank 2:

:<math>
A = 
    \begin{bmatrix}
        34  &  58  &  52 \\
        59  &  89  &  80 \\
        17  &  29  &  26
    \end{bmatrix}.
</math>

If
:<math>
J = \begin{bmatrix}
       2  & 1
    \end{bmatrix},
</math>

then 

:<math>
A = 
    \begin{bmatrix}
       58  & 34 \\
       89  & 59 \\
       29  & 17
    \end{bmatrix}  
    \begin{bmatrix}
        0  &  1  &  \frac{29}{33} \\
        1  &  0  &  \frac{1}{33}
    \end{bmatrix} \approx
    \begin{bmatrix}
       58  & 34 \\
       89  & 59 \\
       29  & 17
    \end{bmatrix}  
    \begin{bmatrix}
        0  &  1  &  0.8788 \\
        1  &  0  &  0.0303
    \end{bmatrix}.  
</math>
